findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of biofilm on the interior of the ice machine. CORRECTED- the ice was covered and the area was wiped with a sanitizing cloth. Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the kitchen’s sanitizer bucket at 10 ppm Chlorine bleach. CORRECTED- the sanitizer was remade, and observed at 100 ppm Cl. Ensure chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are made and tested at a frequency to ensure the concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label (50-200 ppm Cl).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the gaskets at the two door standing freezer (nearest the back door) to be in disrepair, with duct tape holding the gasket to the door. Duct tape is an adhesive, and therefore may degrade. Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. Replace the gaskets by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hand-contact surfaces of the sugar and salt scoops to be touching the food. CORRECTED- the sugar scoop was removed and the salt scoop was placed so that the handle was above the food. Since both sugar and salt are both considered ready to eat (RTE), the scoops must be stored in a way to prevent potential bare hand contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a wet sanitizer cloth on top of the prep cooler on the cooking line. CORRECTED- the cloth was removed from the cook line and placed in the sanitizer bucket by the person in charge. Wet sanitizer cloths should be stored in a sanitizer bucket in-between use to prevent the growth and harborage of mold or bacteria.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw beef being stored on top of sauces directly to the right on the inside of the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Person in charge (PIC) rearranged some produce on the shelves so that raw items are stored underneath produce.  A conversation about storage order took place between the PIC and the inspector. Ensure ready-to-eat (RTE) items are stored above raw items to prevent contamination of RTE items.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
1) The ice machine was observed to contain soil accumulation on the sides within the unit. CORRECTED- employee wiped accumulation with a dry sani-rag. The next time the ice machine is thawing be sure to clean and sanitize the inside of the unit.
2) Inspector observed food debris on knife that was on the magnetic strip at the end of the cook line. CORRECTED- person in charge moved the knife to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure cooking utensils that are stored ready-to-use are clean to prevent cross contamination.

Ensure food contact items are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a wet wiping cloth on top of the prep cooler on the cooking line. CORRECTED- the sani cloth was removed from the line and placed in the sanitizer bucket by the person in charge. Education about wet wiping cloth storage took place between the inspector and person in charge. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer solution when they are not in use.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Food debris and grease accumulation was observed along the cook-line, including but not limited to: under countertops and on shelves, inside the microwave. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of grease, dust, food residue, and other debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
1) Inspector observed a significant amount of rust present on the butchers rack on the left side of the walk-in cooler. Shelves should be cleaned and resealed or replaced so that shelves holding food-contact or non-food-contact items are easy to clean. 
2) Gaskets along the left edge of the walk-in cooler door contain soil accumulation. Wipe edges of gasket to prevent accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
1) Significant amounts of food debris were present underneath the ice machine.
2) Significant amounts of grease were present on the pipes to the left of the hood vent. These pipes are above a food preparation area, and therefore present a risk of contamination.
Deep clean the kitchen to eliminate soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed several personal items (cell phone and wallet on the cook line and a personal drink above the cold holding) stored throughout the facility. Inspector discussed observation with person in charge. Personal items shall be stored in a separate and designated area away from food being served to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from.  [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: A food employee was observed washing their hands at the 3 compartment sink. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who then spoke to the employee. The employee rewashed their hands at the designated handwashing sink. Ensure hands are washed at designated handwashing sinks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.15 FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Raw chicken was observed stored above vegetables in the walk-in cooler. Broccoli was observed stored below raw shrimp in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC rearranged storage so broccoli was not under raw animal proteins. Raw chicken was moved to storage on the bottom shelf, below all other foods. Ensure vegetables are stored above raw animal proteins.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11 (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The kitchen sanitizer bucket was observed with no measurable chlorine concentration. CORRECTED- An employee remade the sanitizer bucket, which was then observed at 200ppm Cl. Ensure sanitizer buckets have 50-200ppm Cl and are changed regularly as they become soiled or sanitizer dissipates.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (A) A chlorine solution shall have a concentration of 50-200ppm. [P]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Three live and several more dead cockroaches were observed on the cookline. Enlist pest control service and deep clean the kitchen. Use glue traps to monitor and identify active areas.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: The gaskets on the 2 door cooler near the back door are duct-taped on. Replace the gaskets so they are fully attached as intended.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11 (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Food debris and grease accumulation was observed along the cookline, including but not limited to: under countertops and on shelves, inside the microwave, and around the rice cooker.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Food debris and soil accumulation was observed under the cookline equipment, along pipes behind the cookline, and under the dish area. Deep clean the kitchen to eliminate soil accumulation and aid in pest control.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
PIC’s allergen awareness training certificate expired at the end of 2024. Ensure all CFMs complete ANSI-approved allergen awareness training.
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment: An employee beverage was observed on the shelf over the short prep cooler in an open container without a lid. CORRECTED- PIC reviewed proper drink storage with staff, and a lid was added to the cup. Store employee drinks in closed containers with a lid and straw to prevent contamination of hands, the container, and food.
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11(B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent contamination of: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: Damp wiping cloths were observed on prep cooler cutting boards and countertops throughout the kitchen. Wiping cloth was placed in bleach solution. Wet/damp wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution between uses.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
The gaskets on the 2 door cooler near the back door are falling off. Replace gaskets so they are fully attached to the cooler. PIC has ordered replacement gaskets.
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. [C]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Facility could not locate their vomit/diarrhea clean up policy. CORRECTED- Inspector printed a new clean up policy. Keep this on file or posted in the kitchen for reference in case vomit or diarrhea clean up is needed in the kitchen.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Cooked tofu was observed stored below raw beef in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Reviewed proper storage order with PIC. Storage was rearranged to store tofu with the vegetables.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment: Time was not tracked for a pan of egg rolls stored above the short prep cooler. A bowl of chicken was observed at 56F in the top of the short prep cooler. PIC indicated that Time as a Control is used for the chicken as well, but no time was noted. Proper tracking of time and discard within 4hrs were discussed. Use sticky notes or another tracking method to record the time foods were removed from cold holding, and ensure they are used or discarded within 4 hours. CORRECTED- Sticky notes were created to reflect the time as a control policy.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19 If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours, food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time frame for use and cannot exceed 4 hours. The food must be served or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when food was removed from temperature control. [Pf]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment: Thawed ROP fish was observed in sealed packages in the bottom of the short prep cooler. The package indicates that fish needs to be removed from the packaging before thawing. Discussed proper thawing, including opening the packages when fish is removed from the freezer.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13 (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Damp wiping cloth observed on the front ledges of both prep coolers. Wiping cloth was placed in bleach solution. Store wiping cloths in sanitizer solution between uses.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
PIC present at the start and end of the inspection has not completed allergen training. A PIC with allergen training arrived early into the inspection and left prior to the completion of the inspection. Ensure all CFMs complete ANSI-approved allergen training. Keep certificates on file for review.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
PIC present at the start of the inspection has an expired CFM certificate. A PIC with a current CFM certificate arrived early in the inspection. Ensure there are enough CFMs on staff to cover all shifts of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
An open can of Monster energy drink was observed on the shelf above the cookline prep cooler. Store personal beverages below or away from food prep areas, and keep beverages in containers with a lid and straw.
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. [C]

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Employee observed placing a lime wedge and shredded lettuce on plate for service with bare hands. CORRECTED- Inspector interrupted the employee and reviewed handling ready-to-eat foods. Employee then used utensils to re-plate the food with lime wedge and shredded lettuce. Ensure ready-to-eat foods are only handled with utensils or clean, gloved hands.
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under  3-301.11(B) and (E). [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw chicken observed above raw beef on a shelf in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Reviewed proper storage order with PIC. Storage was rearranged. Store raw chicken below all other foods to prevent potential cross contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Various foods in the short prep cooler were observed out of temperature (raw chicken, 53F; macaroni salad, 57F; raw steak, 51F; raw pork, 49F; chicken, 48F; and pork, 52F; all probed). CORRECTED- Foods out of temperature will be voluntarily discarded. Foods in the lower portion of the cooler were 41F or below. Monitor cooler temperatures and keep the prep cooler lids closed as much as possible to help foods remain cold.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Employee items (Tums and Tylenol) observed on the shelf above the long prep cooler. CORRECTED- Personal items and medications were moved to a designated storage container where they will not contaminate food or food contact surfaces. (Previously observed during the 9/25/23 inspection). 
7-208.11: (A) First aid supplies that are in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for EMPLOYEES’ shall be labeled properly. (B) Shall be stored in kit or container preventing contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES. [P]
7-207.11: (A) Only medicines for health of EMPLOYEES shall be allowed in ESTABLISHMENT. (B) Medicines shall be labeled and located to prevent contamination to FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) The wall dividing the kitchen from the mop closet (where it was previously damaged) has been partially patched. Complete patch by sealing the edges of the drywall and painting so the wall is smooth, easily cleanable, and nonabsorbent.
2) The countertop backsplash behind the front handwashing sink is warped. Seal or repair to eliminate the gap along the bottom edge of the backsplash.
3) There is a small gap between the dish machine drainboard and the wall. Caulk seal the drainboard to the wall.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Crumb and food debris accumulation observed under the dry storage shelves. Sweep and clean dry storage shelves as often as necessary to keep them clean and to allow easier monitoring for pests.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
PIC present at the start of the inspection has not completed allergen training. A PIC with allergen training arrived early into the inspection. Ensure all CFMs complete ANSI-approved allergen training. Keep certificates on file for review.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
1) Employee observed moving from loading the dish washer to food prep without washing hands. 
2) Employee observed to quickly rinse hands at the dish area spray sink after breading raw meat. CORRECTED- Provided education on handwashing. Ensure employees wash hands with soap and running water at designated handwashing sinks before beginning food prep.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No soap available at the kitchen handwashing sink. CORRECTED- Soap was provided upon inspectors request. Ensure soap is available at all handwashing sinks at all times.
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Employee items (lotion, Tums, and allergy medication) observed on the shelf above the long prep cooler. CORRECTED- Personal items and medications were moved to a designated storage container where they will not contaminate food or food contact surfaces.
7-208.11: (A) First aid supplies that are in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for EMPLOYEES’ shall be labeled properly. (B) Shall be stored in kit or container preventing contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES. [P]
7-207.11: (A) Only medicines for health of EMPLOYEES shall be allowed in ESTABLISHMENT. (B) Medicines shall be labeled and located to prevent contamination to FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES. [P]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
A container bearing a kimchi label was observed full of a white powder. Per PIC, it is baking soda. CORRECTED- PIC labeled container to indicate its contents.
3-302.12: If in working container, FOOD not readily recognized or easily mistakable shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Metal walk-in cooler shelves observed to be soiled with food debris and rust. Clean shelves or replace if necessary.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) Wall dividing the kitchen from the mop closet is damaged, with drywall edges exposed. Patch and repair wall so that it is smooth, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent.
2) Wall to the left of the mop sink observed to be water damaged and possibly beginning to mold. Repair wall.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Bulk breading storage bin was uncovered in the dry storage area. Lid was placed on the storage bin during inspection.
Bulk sugar storage bin was partially uncovered, and the lid for sugar was switched with cornstarch. Sugar was covered with properly labeled lid. Ensure foods are properly covered between uses.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing foods in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Two open gallons of milk observed without labels indicating the dates they were opened. CORRECTED- Per discussion with PIC and staff, open dates were determined and milks were labeled with the dates they were opened. Use or discard within 7 days of opening.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food. [Pf]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Damp wiping cloth observed on the front ledge of the small prep cooler. CORRECTED- Wiping cloth was placed in bleach solution. Proper storage of wiping cloths between uses was discussed.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) Three compartment sink is pulling away from the wall. Gap has been caulked but a gap is still present. Old caulk may need to be removed before repairs can be made. Seal sink to wall.
2) Trim behind the front handwashing sink is warped, leaving gaps that may be uncleanable. Repair or replace front handwashing sink trim.
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: Personal items observed to be intermixed with food and other items used for facility operations in the dry storage area and the prep counter near the walk-in cooler. Owner was advised to continue working on separation of personal items from all other food and products used for food service/operation of the facility. Ensure personal items are stored separate from food/equipment/etc used for service.
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11 Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee entered the kitchen and was observed via the pass-through window going straight to the fryers/cook line without first washing their hands. Literally seconds prior the employee was seated at the designated staff break table in the dining room with the owner (PIC). PIC was advised as to what was observed and stated the employee was planning to wash their hands at the back handwashing sink in the kitchen. Proper handwashing between tasks was discussed. Ensure all staff are washing their hands after breaks before entering the kitchen and prior to food preparation.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 1. Fried vegetable eggrolls were observed in the top holding area of the small prep cooler. Surface temperatures were at 80F. Eggrolls were fried within the last 30 to 45 minutes. PIC moved eggrolls to the walk-in cooler to allow for rapid chilling. 
2. Pan of cooked chicken within the first two hours of cooling was observed covered with plastic wrap in the walk-in cooler. Internal temperature was observed at 68F. Chicken was separated so it was in smaller portions in two pans uncovered in the walk-in cooler to allow for rapid chilling. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

Except when washing fruits and vegetables or when ingredients will be added to food that is being fully cooked/has a kill step for pathogens, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Food separated and protected

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:

Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-305.11 Purses and jackets were observed on dry storage shelving up front on top of and next to cans of soda and boxes of single service items. Proper storage of personal items was discussed. 
Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12 Server washed hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to dispensing paper towels. Server was advised on proper technique and use of a barrier when shutting off the faucet. Server re-washed hands with proper technique before continuing with work. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Cook was observed going between handling soiled and clean dishes without washing hands. Handwashing between tasks was discussed, and cook washed his hands prior to continuing with his next task. 
Food employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after handling soiled equipment or utensils and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11 Panko breading was uncovered in the dry storage area from use over the weekend. Lid was placed on the storage bin.
--Container of peanuts was uncovered on the end of the cook line from use over the weekend. PIC was advised to provide a cover for peanuts when not in use and for long-term, overnight storage (plastic wrap or aluminum foil is ok if lids are not available).
--Containers of food were uncovered in the walkin cooler and in the bottom of the small prep cooler. PIC was advised on covering foods for long-term, overnight storage. Facility is closed on Sunday, so foods should be properly covered at the end of operations on Saturday. If owner comes in on Sunday with her family for dinner, ensure proper covers are placed on foods once dinner is done. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Breading and flour on the ledge above the small prep cooler were observed in soiled pans. PIC noted one pan was left from the weekend while the other two had fresh product added on top of old this morning. Breading and flour were replaced with fresh product in clean pans. Ensure foods are stored in pans that have been cleaned and sanitized between uses. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that have been properly cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the FDA Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Front area sani-bucket was at 0ppm chlorine. Solution was just prepared and was said to have been at proper concentration prior to inspector checking. More bleach was added to bring the solution to 200ppm as directed on label instructions.
A chlorine solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use chlorine test strips to verify concentration.

4-501.114 Sani-bucket in kitchen was observed at a concentration of 100ppm quat. Solution was just prepared; more chemical was added to bring solution to 200ppm as directed on label instructions.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use quat test strips to verify concentration.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Scoop in bulk salt bin was soiled with buildup. Scoop was taken to dish area for ware washing. Clean and sanitize scoops from bulk storage bins daily/when scoops have become soiled from use and handling.
Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is not time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned at any time when contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Cream cheese filling and fried portions of General Tso chicken were without date marks. Products were prepared as of the Saturday prior. Date marking was discussed, and foods were dated.
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Vacuum packaged fish that were received as frozen product were observed thawed in the bottom of the large prep cooler. Labeling on package states to remove fish from packaging prior to thawing under refrigeration. Proper thawing of frozen fish in vacuum packaging was discussed.
Frozen fish that are vacuum packaged (reduced oxygen packaging=ROP) and bear a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use need to be removed from the reduced oxygen environment (packaging) either prior to thawing under refrigeration or prior to, or immediately upon completion of, thawing by other means (e.g. under running water).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Ice scoop was stored on inverted glasses in a dish rack on top of the ice machine. Options for storage of the ice scoop were discussed. PIC noted she would purchased a container for storage or use a container. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, such as ice scoops, shall be stored in a clean, protected location.

Handle of scoop was observed touching salt in the bulk storage bin. Scoop was removed for cleaning and proper storage discussed. Salt is used for cooking and filling salt shakers at the tables, so ensure the scoop is always stored with the handle up out of product. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in food that is not TCS food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) sides and underneath equipment on cook line - fryers, table holding grill, etc. (grease/food debris); and 
B) walkin cooler shelves (general buildup). 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13 Sani-bucket from the weekend was observed at the front service area. PIC noted is was from her family dinner the day prior. Waste water was discarded in the mop sink.
--A puddle of black waste water from mopping was observed in the bottom of the mop bucket. Ensure the all old mop water is discarded at the end of operations daily. Old mop water was discarded.
--Pan of utensils soaking in water was observed with food debris in it. PIC was advised to at minimum discard the soak water and rinse utensils at the end of operations daily. 
Proper disposal of waste water after use was discussed. All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. Properly dispose of all waste water after mopping and when sanitizer solutions are no longer needed. Do not leave utensil soaking water and other waste water sitting in the facility overnight. It could serve as a food/water source for pests.

Clean the walls in the aforementioned areas.

Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean
findings.citation_text:

After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 One cook has an expired food handler certification. Ensure food handler certification is renewed as soon as possible, and provide proof of certification at the next routine inspection. 
All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Person in charge needs to complete the food manager certification course and provide proof of certification by the next routine inspection.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)

Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12, 2-301.14 & 2-301.15 Cook was observed rinsing his hands at the sprayer in the dish area and then proceeded to wipe his hands on his apron prior to retuning to prep area. Cook then handled sliced pineapple prior to returning to the cook line and wiping his hands on wiping cloths. Owner was advised as to what was observed and was asked to have a conversation with the cook on proper handwashing, when to wash hands, and where to wash hands. Cook was later observed properly washing hands at a designated handsink between tasks. Hands were not observed to be wiped on aprons or wiping cloths for the remainder of the inspection. 
Food Employees shall properly clean their hands and exposed portions of their immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Also, hands must be washed after engaging in any activities that contaminate the hands.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Pump bottle for hand soap at the handsink in the kitchen was broken. Another bottle of soap was placed at the handsink to allow for proper handwashing. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:

Inner surface of the package was soiled with food splash, and a piece of dried pepper was observed in the baking powder. Proper storage was discussed, with the option of using a clean, stainless steel pan that can be covered between uses if the original package does not seal properly. Baking powder was placed in a clean container for storage.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Pan of marinated chicken wings was observed on the prep table upon arrival of inspector. Surface temperature was observed at 58F-60F. Wings were just prepared and marinated prior to inspector's arrival based on information provided. Prompt storage of foods to avoid time-temperature abuse was discussed. Wings were portioned in pans and placed in the 2 door freezer for storage. 

Beef, sliced tomatoes, tofu, and noodles in the top holding area of the large prep cooler had internal temperatures at 47F-49F. Owner thought elevated temperatures were due to the lid being open during lunch service. Mahi mahi and scallops in the bottom holding area had internal temperatures of 47F and 48F/50F respectively. A pan of recently prepared raw chicken had an internal temperature of 55F. Cooler was not holding at proper temperature (see #33 for details). All foods that were in use since the start of lunch were to be served or discarded by 5p. Owner chose to discard foods and start with fresh product. Proper use of time control was discussed for temporary storage until cooler is able to maintain foods at 41F/below.

Sweet and sour chicken in the bottom of the small prep cooler was observed with an internal temperature of 47F-48F. Chicken was in a pan that previously up in the top holding area of the cooler but not in direct contact with cold air. Chicken was discarded during the inspection. Owner was advised to cease the practice of stacking pans and containers of food in the top holding areas of coolers. Products that are stacked and not in the holding compartment in direct contact with cold air are less likely to be maintained at 41F/below, especially with frequent opening and closing of cooler lids during busy service times.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 A generic chemical spray bottle hanging on the bottom rung of the dish machine was not labeled as to the contents. Owner thought it was a general cleaning/degreaser used for cleaning general surfaces under and around the dish machine. Owner was advised on proper labeling of chemical spray bottles. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Stem thermometer in the bottom of the large prep cooler used to monitor the temperature was observed above 40F. Thermometer was calibrated with ice water prior to placing it back in the cooler along with inspector's calibrated stem thermometer to verify cold holding temperature. Large prep cooler was observed holding around 48F. Owner called for service and stated a technician should be out sometime later this evening to service the cooler. Do not use the large prep cooler for long-term storage of any TCS food until it is able to maintain foods at 41F/below. 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13 Package of frozen pork was observed in the 3 part sink. Owner noted it was being thawed slightly so it would be easier to cut when preparing pork chops. Owner was advised to thaw it under cold running water or to place it in the walkin cooler until it was able to be sliced for prep. Pork was placed in the walkin cooler to finish thawing.
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Vacuum packaged, completely thawed mahi mahi was observed in the bottom of the large prep cooler.  Proper thawing of vacuum packaged fish was discussed. Owner was advised to make sure packaging is at minimum cut once thawing is complete. Fish were removed from packaging and placed in a pan for storage.
Frozen fish that are vacuum packaged (reduced oxygen packaging=ROP) and bear a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use need to be removed from the reduced oxygen environment (packaging) either prior to thawing under refrigeration or prior to, or immediately upon completion of, thawing by other means (e.g. under running water).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate

A thermometer was not available for checking food temperatures. Obtain and use food thermometers that register temperatures in the range of 0°F-220°F to verify proper cooking, cooling, reheating, hot holding, and cold holding temperatures.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures.

Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

Hood above cook line was also starting to accumulate grease on the baffles. Clean the hood.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Shell eggs in the top of the large cooler were stacked three layers above the rim of the storage pan. Surface temperature was observed at 49°F for eggs stacked on the top. Owner noted eggs are used for several of the dishes, and the top layers of eggs would likely be used before the end of lunch. Owner was advised to discard any of the eggs in question if they were not used by 3p.

Pan with sweet and sour chicken was sitting in the top of the small prep cooler. Chicken was at 51°F. Chicken was stored in the reach-in section of the small prep cooler overnight and just pulled out for lunch. Owner chose to discard the portion of chicken in question.

NOTE: It's a bad practice to stack foods above the rims of containers and to stack pans/containers of food within the top of prep coolers. Products are not maintained as cold when stacked too high or in containers on top of other containers in the top of the cooler.

Cold foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at 41°F/below at all times during storage, display and service.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 -Scoops in bulk powder and panko breading containers were soiled with general buildup on and around the handles. Scoops for cornstarch and flour were stored with soiled handles down in the powders. All scoops were taken to the dish area for ware washing.
Clean and sanitize scoops daily.

Heavily soiled Hoisin sauce can was being reused as a scoop in the bulk rice bin. Hoisin sauce can was discarded in the trash. Only use clean scoops for dispensing foods. Do not reuse #10 cans.

Can openers in prep table drawer were observed with buildup on the blades. Can openers were taken to dish area to go through ware washing. Clean and sanitize can opener and other utensils/equipment between uses.

Fried sweet and sour chicken was observed in a reused scallion box in the walkin cooler. Owner stated too much chicken was made the evening prior, and the chicken in the box was extra. Owner was advised boxes are not considered clean, food grade containers for storage, especially if they came with raw/unwashed produce inside. Owner had staff place chicken in a pan for proper storage.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).

750.510 & 512 - None of the kitchen or wait staff were observed washing hands during the inspection. Wait staff were observed handling soiled dishes, using a wiping cloth from a sani-bucket and getting a drink from personal beverages without washing hands before continuing to the next task.

Cook was observed touching various surfaces with his hands and then having bare hand contact with items such as scallions and basil that were added as garnish and or a final step to dishes and soup after cooking was finished. 

Proper handwashing between tasks and avoiding bare hand contact with ready to eat foods were discussed.
Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, between tasks, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. 
Use clean tongs or spoons for handling garnish and toppings on the cook line.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.800 - Cook was observed rinsing tongs at the 3 part sink and using a wire scrub pad prior to taking the tongs back to the cook line for use. Operator had tongs placed at the dish area to go through a ware washing cycle at the request of the inspector.

To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:

Floors shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean

Walls in the cooking area were soiled with grease and general buildup, especially around the fryer.
Clean the walls and the ceiling vent cover.

Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1280 - Jackets were observed hanging on dry storage shelving. Provide a proper storage area for personal items.

An adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Fried chicken pieces in the top of the small prep cooler were observed at 58°F. Chicken was in a pan stacked on top of pans within the top holding area. Chicken in the top of the cooler would be used or discarded by the end of lunch.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).

findings.comment:

Clean and sanitize utensils between uses to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

Clean general surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly

750.1300 - Bottle labeled floor cleaner had AutoChlor hypochlorite chemical stored inside. Original label was removed; bottle was relabeled appropriately.
Spray bottle of a pinkish colored liquid was observed without a label beneath the dish machine. Operator stated it was a general cleaning solution. Operator labeled the chemical in Chinese for kitchen staff (only persons that use it).

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
