Handwashing must occur at designated handsinks with proper technique between tasks. If hands need to be rinsed then hands should be properly washed.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - Personal drinks were once again observed in the dry storage and kitchen. Drinks were removed upon request of inspector.

Cease the practice of having personal beverages in open glasses and other containers of beverages or plates of food in the kitchen and storage area.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text:
750.1160 - A very small (baby to juvenile size) was observed around the faucet of the back handsink in the kitchen when inspector went to wash hands. It was not possible to determine where it came from exactly. Roach was killed with a paper towel. A similar sized roach was dying in some moisture in a small tub by the handsink, and another similar sized roach was observed on its back on the floor by the freezer across from the handsink. No apparent roach activity was observed in the immediate area. Operator was advised to call for service with a licensed pest control company as soon as possible, and have service with a licensed company before the next routine inspection (see general comments for details)
 
Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Foods in the walkin cooler had surface temperatures at in the mid-forty degree range. Internal temperatures were as follows: chicken 46°F, beef 47°F, and macaroni salad 48°F. Walkin cooler was not holding at proper temperature (see #4). Meats were relocated to freezers for storage. Eggs and a few other products were moved to the fridge that was holding around 40°F. Macaroni salad was discarded at request of inspector.

Foods in the large prep cooler were observed with internal temperatures above 50°F in the top holding area. Foods checked included tofu, beef, and chicken. All were observed at 53°F-56°F. Other products in the bottom and drawers of the large prep cooler were borderline too warm. Tofu in the drawer of the large prep cooler was 45°F. Foods in the top of the large prep cooler were removed and discarded. Fresh product was placed in the top of the large prep cooler.

Cold foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at 41°F/below during storage, display, and service.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Walkin cooler was not holding at proper temperature. Thermometer in the cooler was reading at 40°F but was not accurate. Walkin cooler was not holding at proper temperature. Foods had internal temperatures above 45°F (see #3a). Inspector placed five recently calibrated stem thermometers in the walkin cooler and temperature was observed around 48°F-52°F depending on location of thermometers. A call for service was made, and a technician was scheduled to come in for service on 7/10/18. 
 
Large prep cooler was holding foods above 50°F in the top holding area. The large prep cooler was warm, and it was hard to tell if it was simply temperature abuse due to use (doors not shut properly/top lid open) and the elevated kitchen temperature or if the large prep cooler was also failing. Staff were advised to have technician check the large prep cooler during service on 7/10/18. 
NOTE: It is highly recommended that staff have the refrigeration technician check all cold holding units at time of service.

All refrigeration units used to store TCS foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Waitress rinsed hands and did not use soap to wash hands. Proper handwashing was discussed. 

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
Use soap to later hands and have paper towels ready to dry hands. Once hands have been dried use paper towel as a barrier to shut off the manual faucet.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - Open can of soda and a glass of soda were observed on one of the chest freezers in the dry storage area. Drink was removed from the area.

Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
(R) 750.240 - Three large portions of beef were observed thawing in the first compartment of the 3 part sink. Running water was not being used for the process. Cold running water was turned on and placed over the thawing portions of beef.
This is the second inspection in a row where improper thawing was observed. Cease the practice of leaving thawing foods in the sink, and do not place them in pans of water. Use cold running water as foods are thawing in the sink, and when possible, plan a head and thaw foods in the walkin cooler overnight, keeping in mind that larger pieces of meat may take several days to thaw under refrigeration.

Foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be properly thawed by one of the  following methods: 1. Under refrigeration at 41°F/below, 2. Under potable running water 70°F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Breading and flour observed on the shelf above the small prep cooler had buildup along the top and inner edges of storage pans. Also, old meat was observed mixed in a couple of the products. Products in question were discarded. Clean pans with fresh breading and flour were put out for use.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Sift breading and flour up to every 4hrs, and switch out pans as they become soiled and at the end of operations daily.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Owner washed hands and then touched the handle of the paper towel dispenser to retrieve paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed, with the option of using a forearm to touch the handle of the paper towel dispenser if the paper towels are not already dispensed and ready to use. 

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. Avoid touching the handle of the paper towel dispenser with freshly washed hands by using a forearm to dispense paper towels or dispense paper towels prior to beginning the handwashing process. Use paper towels as a barrier to shut off the faucet once hands are dried.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Sanitizer concentration at the dish machine was 0ppm chlorine. During a full cycle of the dish machine it was determined the sanitizer was not dispensing from the chemical tube. Owner tried priming the line, but it did not appear to help. A call for service was made, and the technician advised the owner to prime the line for 2 minutes to see if that helped. Sanitizer began dispensing from the line, and the dish machine was observed at 50-100ppm chlorine upon correcting the issue.

All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Damp wiping cloth was observed on the prep cooler at the cook line. Towel was used to wipe down the front ledge of the cooking equipment and the front of the prep cooler but not placed back in the sani-bucket. Staff placed wiping cloth in bleach solution upon request of inspector. 

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Soap was not available at the front handsink upon arrival of inspector. Soap was placed at the front handsink.

Soap was barely coming out of the women's room soap dispenser. Dispenser was empty. Owner placed soap in the dispenser.

A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory. Maintain soap and paper towels at all handsinks to allow for proper handwashing.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.citation_text:
750.100 - Bamboo shoots (2) and tomato ketchup (1) with severe dents along and near can seams were stocked in the dry storage room available for use. All damaged cans were pulled and set aside to be returned to the supplier for credit.
NOTE: Do not stock dented cans for use. If dents are present along the seams or severe dents are located anywhere on the cans, then products must not be used for food service. When cans are damaged the product inside could be unsafe to eat.

Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - Chicken was observed thawing in a tub of standing water. Operator moved the tub of chicken to the 3 part sink and placed it under cold running water.

Foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be properly thawed by one of the  following methods: 1. Under refrigeration at 41°F/below, 2. Under potable running water 70°F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.280 - Rice scoop was observed in a pan of water at the steam table. The temperature of the water holding the scoop was ~120°F. Operator stated she just added some new water to the pan within the hour. The water in the steam table was at 138°F but was barely in contact with the rice scoop pan in the steam table. The temperature of the steam table was adjusted higher and more hot water was added to help raise the temperature for the rice scoop storage water.

Maintain the rice scoop storage water at 135°F/above at all times.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.512 - Employee did not wash hands upon returning to the front service area after leaving the restroom. Facility has a sign posted at the handsink in the front service area stating "all employees must rewash hands after leaving the restroom". Restrooms have only air drying devices and no paper towels. Handwashing policy was revisited with operators.
NOTE: The cooks working at the time of inspection were observed washing hands between tasks and utilizing proper technique.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. Employees also need to adhere to the handwashing policy posted at the front handsink pertaining to rewashing hands upon entering the work area after leaving the restroom.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Prep table in back was wiped off with a cloth that was not previously stored in a sani-bucket. Bleach solution was prepared for the kitchen (100ppm), and wiping cloths were placed in the solution for storage.
NOTE: Always use wiping cloths from bleach solutions for wiping down prep tables and other general surfaces in the kitchen.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The fire suppression system over the wok was observed to have grease and dust buildup. Areas in question were cleaned during the inspection.

Maintain the fire suppression system in a clean and sanitary condition. It is directly over the cook line and buildup from the system could fall into food being prepared for customers if buildup becomes excessive and chunky.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - Buildup of grease and food debris was observed on the sides of equipment between the wok, flat grill, and fryer. Clean the general surfaces between cook line equipment as needed to eliminate buildup of grease and food debris. Consider having a company help with steam cleaning.

Clean general surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - A) Pans of flour and panko breading on the back ledge of the small prep cooler had food debris buildup, and a small portion of dried egg was observed in panko breading. Also, tupperware holding wontons in the bottom of the small prep cooler was soiled. Storage containers were changed out during the inspection.
Change out breading/flour pans and tupperware for storage of foods at minimum daily. Clean and sanitize containers between uses, and sift breading up to every 4 hours if not more frequently to remove proteins (egg, chicken, etc.) from product.

B) Soiled knives were observed on magnetic knife strip. Knives were placed through dish machine during inspection. Make sure all knives are going through full ware washing process after use. Do not store soiled knives on the knife strip for potential use. Clean and sanitize the knife strip daily/as needed. 
Knives used for opening food packaging need to be cleaned and sanitized at minimum at the end of operations daily; unless food debris gets on the knives, then they need to be cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.280 - Scoop handles were observed down in products in the bulk powder (sugar, flour, etc.) and panko breading bins. Scoops were repositioned to allow for proper storage with handles up out of products.   

Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.510 & 514 - 1. Employee was observed rinsing hands at the 3 part sink. Employees were advised to use only designated handsinks for handwashing. Staff were observed washing hands at the handsinks for the remainder of the inspection.
2. Employees were washing hands but barriers were not being used properly. Handles of faucets and paper towel dispenser were touched after process was completed. Proper handwashing technique was discussed; educational handout was provided.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment. Hands must only be washed at designated handsinks.
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - Cook was observed eating in the dry storage room. Owner had cook move to designated break area out in the dining room to finish eating.

Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b -A)  Meat grinder was observed soiled with food debris. Owner noted meats are cut with a knife by hand. Items such as fresh ginger, garlic, etc. are prepared with the grinder. 
Clean and sanitize all parts of the grinder at minimum at the end of operations daily. All the parts that can be removed must go through the dish machine for ware washing, and all other parts must be manually washed, rinsed, and sanitized.

B) Magnetic knife strip was soiled with general buildup and some food debris. Clean and sanitize the magnetic knife strip throughout the day, and maintain it clean.

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Kitchen handsink basin had an empty #10 can and a large piece of blue plastic in it. Items were removed and discarded to allow for proper access of the handsink.

Handsinks are to be accessible at all times to allow for proper handwashing.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Grease buildup was observed on the wall along the top of the large black pipe behind the cooking equipment. Clean the walls and attached pipes as needed, and maintain them clean.

Walls and attached equipment shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1300 - Bleach for preparing sanitizer bucket solutions was observed in an old rice wine bottle. Bottle was not labeled as to the contents. A label was provided during the inspection. (See general comments)

Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - A) Dozens of chicken breasts were delivered prior to the arrival of inspector. All of the chicken was observed out at ambient temperature being processed. Surface temperatures were observed at 50F-55F. Several portions in pans were wrapped and placed in the freezer. One portion was in the process of being cut up for use and was immediately placed in the walkin cooler after prep was completed.
Staff were advised to only keep out and work with the amount of food needed in the moment. Do not leave pounds and pounds of product sitting out while working with only a small portion. 

B) Foods in the prep coolers had varying temperatures in the forty degree range depending on location. Tofu in the drawer of the large prep cooler had an internal temperature of 43F, while chicken in the top holding area of the large cooler had an internal temperature of 48F. Bean sprouts in the same cooler were observed to be sitting in liquid with an internal temperature of 42F. Chicken in the small prep cooler had an internal temperature of 46F. Egg rolls in the bottom of the small prep cooler that were just fried within the last few hours had surface temperatures of 51F. Proper use of coolers to avoid temperature abuse was discussed, including refraining from placing hot foods in the coolers and keeping lids closed between use. Manager adjusted the thermostat of the small prep cooler to a slightly colder setting.

C) Noodles sitting out on the large prep cooler were observed at 75F. Noodles were out since about noon according to information provided. Noodles were to be used or discarded by 4p.

Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage, display and service.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text:
750.140(b) - Macaroni noodles were observed cooling on top of the chest freezer in the storage area. Surface and internal temperatures were at 64F. Date and time were not labeled on the container to indicate when cooling began. Staff indicated the noodles were prepared around 130p with boiling water, and noodles were rinsed with cold water prior to being placed in the strainer in the storage area. Noodles were placed in a storage bin and moved to the walkin cooler to finish cooling.  

Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in 4 hrs. Label cooling foods with date and time of preparation, and use clean, calibrated stem thermometers to monitor the temperature of cooling foods to ensure they reach benchmark temperatures in designated time frame for proper cooling.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - A) Scoops in bulk powder bins were soiled with heavy buildup of old food debris on handles and the areas immediately beneath the handles. Manager was asked how often scoops are cleaned, and she thought they might have been cleaned some time in the past two weeks. Scoops were removed to be cleaned and sanitized.

B) Clean, cut vegetables were observed uncovered in the walkin cooler. The shelf above was soiled, and debris was hanging down over the uncovered containers of food. Containers of vegetables were covered during the inspection.

C) Meat grinder food contact surfaces were soiled with buildup of old food debris. Clean and sanitize the meat grinder between uses.

Foods shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses, and clean general surfaces daily.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Staff were not washing hands between tasks, and when observed washing hands proper technique was not used. Inspector demonstrated proper handwashing technique for kitchen staff.

Employees must properly wash hands between tasks, any time hands may have been contaminated, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - All general surfaces throughout the facility need to be cleaned including shelving, inside and outside surfaces of coolers and freezers, and all cooking equipment.

Clean general surfaces daily to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.citation_text:
750.600 - Empty oyster sauce cans were being reused. Manager was advised to cease the practice of re-using #10 food cans. Discard all empty #10 cans.

Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1280 - Employee jacket was observed hanging on the shelving in dry storage next to/above food items. Provide employees with a place to store personal belonging separate from food preparation and food storage areas.

An adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.citation_text:
750.1310 - Bottles of butane fuel were observed on the top shelf stored over foods in the dry storage area. Butane fuel was moved to a proper storage area away from food.

All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1300 - Bleach was being stored in an old rice wine bottle, and a spray bottle of general cleaner hanging in the dish area was not labeled. Containers were labeled as to the contents during the inspection.

Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-250 Observed fried chicken in a pot stored on top of the small prep cooler. Chicken was probed at 53F. Chicken was found to be from lunch service. Item was allowed to be cooled in the reach-in freezer.  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: 750-140(b)  Observed cooked noodles, covered and being stored in the walk-in cooler. Noodles did not have a time indicated on the food. The food was covered and observed in a large container. Noodles were apparently cooked at 1:00pm. During the inspection, the noodles were re-portioned into smaller containers and left uncovered into the cooler.  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: 750-1170 Observed the back door to be opened. Screen door is not tight fitting. Outside door was closed during the inspection. The screen door should be repaired to be self closing and tight-fitting. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-250 Observed the Coca Cola cooler to be holding temperature at 52F (probed air temperature). Milk is the only potentially hazardous food in the cooler. It was discarded during the inspection. Cooler was being repaired during the inspection. Additional milk is being stored in the walk-in cooler.  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750-250 The walk-in cooler is stocked with meat, eggs, and vegetables. Most of the cooler is full of uncut, non-PHF veggies. Several of the meats were in the process of thawing from the frozen state so an understanding of whether or not the walk-in unit was failing was difficult to asses. Steak on the middle shelf was probed at 50F, chicken further forward on that same shelf was probed at 52F. Macaroni salad on the top shelf in the far back was probed at 48F. Air temperature is apparently 48F. The cooler was checked in the morning and was around 36F. Discussed if poor temperatures are a result of defrost or just improper cooling. Walk-in cooler was just serviced a few weeks ago.
The long preparation cooler is holding foods at 50F on the top and 48F in the base (tofu = 48F (probed), tomatoes = 50 (probed), fish = 49 (probed), chicken = 53 (probed)). Foods were stocked high within the cooler. Discussed stocking foods too far in advance of service. The kitchen is incredibly warm and cannot keep up with the opening and closing of the cooler lid - especially when the foods are piled over the top of the containers. Cease overstocking foods in the preparation coolers. This cooler was also checked this morning and was below 40F. Discussed calibrating stem thermometer. 
All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: 750-140(b)  Observed a ten gallon bucket of cooling teriyaki sauce covered, at 124F, and with no time indicated on container being stored in the walk-in cooler. Owner suggested this bucket of hot sauce was the cause of the warm walk-in cooler. Bucket was left uncovered during the inspection. Cooling hot items should be conducted in a very active manner. Use an ice bath or an ice wand to help with the cooling of hot foods. The time must be indicated on the container so that time/temperature benchmarks can be monitored. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510a Observed an employee switch tasks from food handling, to maintenance, and return to food handling without proper handwashing. Discussed handwashing with staff. Wash hands between tasks. Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Observed the handles of the preparation cooler doors to be soiled with food and grease. Also, the freezer of the white, upright unit is observed soiled with crumbs. Clean the handles and freezer. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-850 The drawer in the preparation counter to the left of the white upright freezer is observed soiled with food splash. Clean the drawer and the soiled utensils within.  Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: 750-1170 The back door has a serious gap beneath the left side. Weather stripping was recently purchased but could not be produced during the inspection. Provide a proper sweep or weather stripping to eliminate the gap beneath this door. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: 750-1280 Observed a purse, pink coat, and a shirt stored on the shelves in the hallway leading to the mop sink. Cease storing personal items on these shelves that are also holding food and single-service items. There is a shelf in the dry storage room and a shelf in the frontline that hold personal items.  Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750-250  There were several foods probed to be out of temperature in the large preparation cooler. Beef on the top was probed at46F and noodles also on the top were probed at 48F. The noodles were recently pulled from the walk-in cooler and allowed to rest on top of the containers of the prep cooler. Noodles were moved to the base of the prep cooler during the inspection. The lid of the preparation cooler was closed to aide in cold holding. Discussed keeping the preparation lid closed when the facility is not busy. All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.
750-151(a) Observed a gallon of milk without proper date marking. Manager indicated milk was opened on Monday. Properly date mark foods with the date they are opened within 24 hours of opening.  Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510a Observed an employee switch tasks from cutting raw fish to aiding with cooking without washing hands between activities. Neither cook was observed washing hands frequently. Discussed hand washing with manager. Educate staff on the importance of handwashing. Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-650a Observed the pitcher of the blender to be cracked and damaged and repaired with tape. Cease use of this blender. There is a new blender available. Discard the old one and start using the new one. Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Wet wiping cloths are observed resting on the cutting board of the preparation cooler. There is a sani-bucket available on the frontline but not one available for the backline. Store wet wiping cloths in sani-solution between uses. Discussed the use of a stem thermometer when checking temperatures. A sani-bucket with cloth should be available for wiping stem thermometer between uses. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) Observed a bowl coated with flour from Monday. Mixing bowl is used to coat foods with powder. Bowl should be removed daily for cleaning. Bowl was pulled during inspection for cleaning. Several bowls are available for the various mixing of foods. Depending on the food being mixed the bowls should be removed for proper cleaning at least every four hours.
